transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-02
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Gupta (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Kumo Head of Platform), Priya Nair (Kumo SRE), Liam O'Connor (CTO)

---
Summary: handoff from AE -> SE to scope POC traffic topology + bench plan.

00:00 Avery: okay hi everyone thanks for joining. this is Avery from Redwood inference, i'm joined by Maya our solutions engineer. quick roll call?
00:08 Diego: hi Diego here, head of platform at Kumo.
00:11 Priya: Priya, SRE team.
00:13 Liam: Liam O'Connor, CTO.
00:16 Maya: Maya, solutions eng, nice to meet you all.

01:02 Avery: quick agenda - we want to confirm what success looks like, get a snapshot of your traffic shape — qps, burstiness, concurrency — token lengths for inputs and outputs, then agree bench plan and timeline.
01:20 Diego: yeah our main ask is prove we can run with equivalent latencies to our current microservice and hit cost targets. we're sensitive to tail latency on peak.
01:35 Priya: also privacy and VPC peering, we'll need SAML SSO and a SOC2 artifact before infra tests.
01:42 Maya: understood. we'll share our security pack; that's standard. for the bench we'll need traffic replay samples and a small synthetic harness.

04:05 Diego: so baseline numbers — currently our chat system does about 110 steady qps globally, peaks up to 320 for 5-10 minutes during promo windows. typical concurrency from our app side is 35-60 concurrent requests depending on region.
04:28 Maya: okay that burst pattern is helpful. can you confirm average input token length and response sizes?
04:34 Diego: average user prompt is about 32 tokens (we strip metadata) and responses average 140 tokens, but we have a long-tail — about 5% of responses > 600 tokens for multi-turn context.
04:48 Liam: and we do a few function calls and structured outputs for checkout flows which can blow tokens.
04:55 Maya: good — so token mix: input ~32, output median ~140, p95 ~400, 5% > 600. noted. that affects KV cache hit and runtime memory.

07:10 Avery: what are your SLA targets for the POC? do you have pass/fail thresholds?
07:16 Diego: we want p95 latency under 400ms for common flows and error rate <0.5% for 30-day equivalent load. cost-wise, we need to show less than 30% uplift vs our current CPU-only stack at our projected volume.
07:31 Maya: okay p95 400ms, error <0.5% and cost target. for Redwood we usually map to p50/p95/p99 — we'll aim to surface p95 and tail.

09:00 Priya: for security gating we'll need SOC2, encryption at rest with our KMS, and logs to go into our SIEM via syslog or S3. can Redwood do customer-managed KMS in the private deployment?
09:18 Maya: yes, on Private we support customer KMS/HSM. for Dedicated hosted we can integrate with partner KMS; we'll include details in the security pack.

11:45 Maya: bench plan idea: phase 0 — collect traffic samples and session traces (you); phase 1 — synthetic replay at small scale to validate harness; phase 2 — sustained ramp to steady qps and controlled bursts to simulate promo; phase 3 — long-run stability and quantization/batching knob tuning; deliverable — bench report + cost model and recommended config. we think 3-4 weeks.
11:59 Diego: that lines up. can you run both Hosted API and Dedicated profiles so we can compare economics?
12:09 Maya: yes, we'll run model variants and quantization configs. note models with larger context will change throughput. we'll capture tokens/sec and GPU utilization.

15:20 Avery: specifics: what QPS should we target in the bench? you said 110 steady, 320 peak — any other region splits?
15:28 Diego: primary US-west region covers ~60% of traffic, EU is 30%, rest 10%. for bench let's mirror US-west heavy profile: steady 120 qps, 4x minute-long spikes to 320 qps, concurrency nominal 45. also one long-chat cohort: 5% sessions with avg outputs 800 tokens to stress memory/KV.

18:05 Maya: good. we'll design a scenario with three cohorts: short (60% requests, input 20-40 tokens, output 60-160), medium (35%, input 40-80, output 160-400) and long-tail (5%, output 600-1200). we'll provide the load generator config and the histogram to map token distribution.

22:34 Priya: about replay — our traces are gzipped session logs, can you ingest them? they contain some PII but we can scrub. we prefer a synthetic approximation for compliance.
22:48 Maya: we can accept scrubbed logs or you can provide aggregated histograms. best is synthetic replay derived from your histograms plus a small scrubbed sample for fidelity checks.

26:11 Liam: timeline question: can Redwood commit to the 4-week POC with weekly checkpoints? we're aiming for exec review end of March.
26:21 Avery: yes, 4 weeks is feasible. suggested timeline: week 0-1 sample + harness, week 2 bench runs and tuning, week 3 long-stability and cost tuning, week 4 analysis + report. target exec review 2027-03-25 (tentative).

29:00 Diego: any limitations on model sizes/sequence length? we rely on 2k context for multi-turn.
29:06 Maya: we support up to 4k in most model variants; throughput will drop as context grows. we'll capture tokens/sec and request latency at 2k. also discuss prefix/KV caching to reduce repeated context re-sends for the same session.

33:40 Priya: logging and observability — we'll want per-route latency, tokens per request, token cost breakdown; can Redwood provide tracing hooks?
33:51 Maya: yes console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdown and trace IDs. we'll include a dashboard example.

37:50 Diego: what's the expected GPU footprint for steady 120 qps with median output 140 tokens? rough ballpark.
37:56 Maya: rough back-of-envelope: with a mid-tier optimized 8-GPU pool and batching at small latency SLO we might run 120 qps with ~4-6 GPUs depending on model and quant. but we'll get precise numbers during the bench runs. we'll produce a sizing table (qps vs GPUs vs cost).

41:10 Avery: competitors — you mentioned vendor evals?
41:15 Liam: we looked at Anthropic pricing and VendorX managed endpoints; main tradeoff is control + observability vs marginal price differences.
41:27 Maya: we'll include a comparative note focused on latency and tail behavior.

45:05 Diego: success criteria recap — p95 <400ms, error <0.5%, cost uplift <30% vs current, demonstrate VPC peering or Private deployment for security.
45:20 Avery: yep agree. we'll scope both Hosted and Dedicated scenarios and show fallback profile.

50:00 Maya: a couple of practical asks: can you provide a small sample set (1000 anonymized requests) and a 24-hour aggregate histogram of qps and token counts? that will let us seed the replay harness.
50:12 Diego: yes we'll export that by week.
50:22 Priya: security questionnaire — we'll nominate a point person and share SSO metadata.
50:28 Diego: i'll own traffic samples; Priya will handle security. we'll aim to have both items in the next 5 business days.

56:40 Avery: next steps and owners: send security pack and SOC2, share bench template, schedule workshop.
56:50 Maya: i'll send the load generator repo (link) and benchmark spreadsheet.

60:00 Liam: thanks all, feels good. quick recap in email please and include tentative slot for the 2-hour workshop.
60:12 Avery: will do. thanks everyone.

---
Notes: rough transcription; some names/tokens may be misrecognized. Links referenced: (benchmark spreadsheet) https://redwood.example.com/benchmarks/ke-template, (load generator) https://github.com/redwood/load-replay, (security pack) https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2.pdf
